version.changelog: Add structured metadata for ClawHub trust review

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (inject run-only secrets into subprocesses) aligns with the declared requirements, but it asks for real secret credentials and instructs running arbitrary subprocesses with those secrets—relying on operator-supplied 'run-only' tokens and agent discipline—creating a realistic risk of secret exfiltration or misuse.

dimensions.detail: Name/description require the authy binary and AUTHY_TOKEN/AUTHY_KEYFILE which is consistent with a secret-injection helper. The declared binaries and env vars match the stated purpose; nothing extraneous is requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md tells the agent to run arbitrary commands via `authy run` (e.g., curl, node, pytest) with secrets injected into the subprocess environment. That is necessary for the tool's purpose, but it also means the agent can execute any command that could leak secrets (network calls, writing to files, child processes). The doc also contains operator commands like `authy get`/`export` (labeled 'Not for Agents') which, if used or if a non-run-only token is provided, would expose secret values. The skill relies on external operational constraints (use of run-only tokens and limited scopes) rather than enforcing them.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec or bundled code — lowest install risk. It requires an `authy` binary already present but does not install anything itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requires two environment variables (AUTHY_TOKEN, AUTHY_KEYFILE), which is proportionate for a CLI that authenticates to a secrets service. However, these are credentials/secrets themselves; the SKILL.md recommends 'run-only' tokens but cannot enforce that. AUTHY_KEYFILE could be a path to a private key — the skill does not declare any required config paths, so permissions and file access are left to the operator.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No always:true, no install-time persistence, and default model invocation allowed (normal). The skill does not request system-wide configuration changes or persistent privileges beyond requiring the authy binary and env vars.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose, but it handles real credentials and lets the agent run arbitrary commands with those credentials injected. Before installing: (1) verify the origin and integrity of the `authy` binary (install only from a trusted release/source); (2) only provide least-privilege, short-lived 'run-only' tokens and tightly scoped policies; (3) avoid giving the agent network or arbitrary command execution privileges if you don't fully trust it (consider disabling autonomous invocation for this skill or limiting agent permissions); (4) store AUTHY_KEYFILE securely and ensure file permissions restrict access; (5) audit any commands the agent runs with `authy run` to ensure they cannot exfiltrate secrets. If you cannot guarantee token type, scope, and binary provenance, treat this skill as high-risk.
